name: r6-m11
statement: Because the prompt asks for an 'Answer:' line, the cued base sometimes writes its answer marker before half of its text is written and then spends the rest justifying that value without re-deriving it; these premature commitments are wrong far more often than late-stated answers and make up a large share of the base's quick finished-wrong answers, while RL, which boxes once at the end, rarely commits early.
scope: Covers the cued Olmo-3-1025-7B base on MATH-500 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 (stored T1 rows), finished answers only, and RL-Zero-Math 3.1 plain (T2) as the case where the effect should be absent. It explains a small slice of the gap: the quick finished-wrong answers (on the order of 13 to 30 problems), not cap hits, not the long-answer errors that dominate hard328, and not wrong plans on problems the base never solves. It does not claim the 'Answer:' format is worse on average (see conflicts) and makes no claim about T 0.6 looping cells.

imports.finding: Committing to the answer field before the reasoning (answer-first order) collapses multi-step arithmetic accuracy at unchanged reasoning length, most in small models.
imports.how: Supplies the causal step: an answer written before the derivation is a guess that the following text rationalises, so early-marker answers should be wrong more often at equal length and their value should survive the text after them.

explains.how: Quick base answers can be wrong because a committed early value is justified instead of derived, which RL, boxing only after its derivation, does not do (0 wrong at <= 4,000).

explains.quote: the base ends with an 'Answer:' line in 39-46 % of answers
explains.how: The base follows the prompt's 'Answer:' request often, which is the channel through which an answer line can be written before the work is done.

explains.quote: 6 of 11 base slips read are followed by a check that repeats the slip
explains.how: Checks after a committed value restate it rather than re-derive it, which is the justification half of the mechanism.

explains.quote: Intrinsic self-review fixes no math on MATH-500 for base or RL
explains.how: Once a value is committed, further text by the same model defends it, so appended review changes no math answer.

explains.quote: First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer.
explains.how: Base errors sit early in the text, where a premature commitment would put them, rather than accumulating toward the end.

conflicts.how: Answers in the 'Answer:' format are about 92 % right, more than boxed ones, so the 'Answer:' request does not lower accuracy on average; the mechanism must hold only for the early-positioned subset, which this item does not separate.

conflicts.quote: base slip 35% [24, 48], wrong plan 28%, misread 23%, format 13%
conflicts.how: A blind judge classed base errors as derivation slips, plans and misreads, with no category for an answer stated before its derivation; either the judge folds premature commitment into these labels or it is rare.

rival: Slip-and-difficulty account (r5-m02 / result-f21d2e line): base wrong answers come from slips, misreads and hard problems in an ordinary derive-then-state order; an early marker is just a provisional intermediate candidate on long, hard answers that keep searching. It predicts that early-marker wrong answers usually change value later (first marker equal to the final answer in about half of them), that quick wrong answers sit in the early group no more often than quick right answers do, and that banning answer markers right after the commit point does not raise accuracy. The theory predicts the early value is kept (about 0.8), that early commitments make up a large share of quick wrong answers, and that delaying the marker helps.

predictions.experiment: Wrong-rate ratio of early-marker to late-marker finished answers of the cued base at T 1.0 (MATH-500, T1).
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl, 500 rows). Keep rows with cap_hit false. v3_last = grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py, the score_v3 procedure) on the full text against gold, recomputed. First marker = whichever starts earliest in text: (a) a line whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:' (start = index of the 'A'; end = end of that line, or end of text), (b) the first '\boxed{' (start = index of the backslash; end = index just after its brace-balanced closing '}', or end of text if unbalanced). Drop rows with no marker. f = start / len(text). Early group: f < 0.5 AND len(text) - end > 300. Late group: every other kept row. wrong rate = (rows with v3_last == 0) / rows, per group. Statistic = wrong rate(early) / wrong rate(late). If the late rate is 0 and the early rate > 0 the statistic is +infinity; if the early group has fewer than 15 rows the prediction counts as refuted. One row per problem; no ties arise.
predictions.refuted_by: statistic below 1.3, or early group with fewer than 15 rows

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: among the cued base's early-marker finished-wrong T1 answers, the share whose final answer equals the first-marker value. Answer-first commitment predicts the early value is kept (about 0.8). The nearest rival (slip/difficulty: an early marker is a provisional candidate on a long searching answer) predicts the value is usually revised, about 0.4-0.5.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. Use exactly the cap_hit filter, v3_last, first marker (start, end, content), f and early-group rule of the previous recipe. First-marker content: for an 'Answer:' line, the rest of that line after 'Answer:'; for '\boxed{', the brace-balanced contents. Final answer = the answer string that grader v3's extraction returns for the full text. Keep early-group rows with v3_last == 0 and a non-empty final answer. same = 1 iff grader v3's equivalence function, applied to the string 'Answer: ' + content as the response and the final answer string as the gold, returns right; else 0. Statistic = mean of same over kept rows. If fewer than 8 rows are kept the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: statistic below 0.6, or fewer than 8 kept rows

predictions.experiment: Cause share: of the cued base's quick finished-wrong T1 answers (at most 2,000 generated tokens), the fraction that are early-marker answers. The rival (slow-reasoning slips stated at the end) puts few of them in the early group.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. Keep rows with cap_hit false, n_generated <= 2000 and v3_last == 0 (v3_last recomputed as in the first recipe). A kept row is early if it has a first marker and meets the early-group rule of the first recipe (f < 0.5 and more than 300 characters after the marker's end); rows with no marker count as not early and stay in the denominator. Statistic = early kept rows / kept rows. If fewer than 8 rows are kept the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: statistic below 0.2, or fewer than 8 kept rows

predictions.experiment: Where the effect should be absent: share of RL's finished plain T 1.0 answers (T2) that are early-marker answers.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl, 500 rows). Keep rows with cap_hit false. Apply the first-marker definition and early-group rule of the first recipe (f < 0.5 and len(text) - end > 300). Rows with no marker are kept and count as not early. Statistic = early rows / kept rows. No grading needed.

predictions.experiment: GPU: re-continue the cued base from just before its early commitment. Take every T1 row (base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl) that is in the early group of offline prediction 1 and has v3_last == 0. Prefix = cue prompt + text[:start of first marker]. Continue with the base, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384 minus prefix tokens, 4 samples per prefix, two arms with the same seeds: (A) unconstrained; (B) logit bias -100 on every vocabulary token whose decoded string, stripped, equals 'Answer' or contains 'boxed', for the first 512 new tokens only, then unconstrained. Grade each continuation (prefix text + continuation) with grader v3. Statistic = right rate(B) - right rate(A), pooled over all continuations. The slip rival predicts about 0 (the same wrong value comes back later).
predictions.unit: difference in fraction of continuations right
predictions.refuted_by: arm B minus arm A at or below 0.05
